items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-09-04
items.q: And Mrs. Rankin can remind me if I'm slow on it.

ctx.x: This is an interview with Bill Russell at Seminar Room 2 in the Harvard Tilton Memorial Library at Tulane University. This is Rio 1, the date is September 4th, 1962.

We'd been talking about some of the, this is Bill Russell again, some of the musicians that I'd interviewed at various times preparing for the book Jazz Man, and other times after that, that we weren't able to talk to because most of them are dead now. We weren't able to interview them for our Jazz Archive directly here. One of them was George Bach K., whom I stopped to see in Philadelphia in 1940, fall of 1940. The actual date was December 15th, 1940, on the way when I was moving to Pittsburgh. And he was…

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-08-31
items.q: but a note here to Mrs. Rankin or whoever hears this later.

ctx.x: The early ones are not available?

No, at best. And also, I have a note here I noticed right here in front of me. I think the 1919 and 1920 files were missing, even in 1938 when I went there, in December of 1938. But I have some of these notes, which I'll go over, and might be able to enlarge a little bit on them. These are rather sketchy. Put on ahead. I mean, I'll send them down to Missouri. I see. Because it's a job that's going to take hours and days to go over that. And I'll copy it out, and it'll have to be by longhand, and I'll send a…
There's also a lot of material there that's invaluable. And we ought to be sure and get recorded some way.
